insights.claim: odh-model-controller uses a dual-deployment architecture: a controller-runtime manager and a separate model-serving-api HTTP server, each with distinct authentication models.
insights.reasoning: The analyzer identifies two Deployment workloads (odh-model-controller and model-serving-api). Source inspection reveals the model-serving-api server implements Bearer token authentication via its own middleware, while the controller-runtime manager uses TokenReview/SubjectAccessReview for metrics. This split means authentication failures in one deployment do not affect the other.

insights.claim: All 8 admission webhooks use failurePolicy: Fail, prioritizing correctness over availability for model serving resources.
insights.reasoning: The analyzer extracted 5 mutating and 3 validating webhooks, all with Fail policy. This fail-closed design means webhook unavailability blocks Pod creation, InferenceService updates, and NIM Account changes cluster-wide. Operators should ensure webhook Deployment availability to avoid blocking legitimate resource mutations.

insights.claim: The model-serving-api /metrics endpoint on port 8080 is TLS-encrypted but lacks application-level authentication, unlike the controller-runtime /metrics endpoint which uses TokenReview + SubjectAccessReview.
insights.reasoning: The controller-runtime metrics endpoint at :8443/metrics applies WithAuthenticationAndAuthorization filters, but the model-serving-api metrics at :8080/metrics uses promhttp.Handler() directly behind TLS without authentication. Any client with network access to port 8080 can scrape metrics. In a zero-trust network model, this is an authentication gap relative to the controller metrics.
